subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 62-year-old woman reports 3 weeks of pain and stiffness in her shoulders and hips that is worst in the morning. She has low-grade fever, malaise, and has lost 4 kg. Physical examination shows no muscle weakness; strength is 5/5 throughout. Laboratory studies show ESR 78 mm/h, elevated CRP, and a normal creatine kinase.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Polymyalgia rheumatica causes proximal shoulder and hip girdle pain and stiffness in females older than 50, often with fever, malaise, and weight loss. It does not cause true muscle weakness, and laboratories show elevated ESR and CRP with a normal CK. There is a rapid response to low-dose glucocorticoids, and it is associated with giant cell (temporal) arteritis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Fibromyalgia causes chronic widespread pain with tender points, fatigue, poor sleep, and normal inflammatory markers; it lacks fever, weight loss, and an elevated ESR.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polymyositis causes progressive symmetric proximal weakness with an elevated CK and endomysial CD8+ inflammation, not pain-only stiffness with a normal CK.
explanation_incorrect.D: Dermatomyositis includes proximal weakness, an elevated CK, and characteristic rashes such as Gottron papules and heliotrope eyelid edema.
explanation_incorrect.E: Myositis ossificans is a post-traumatic painful soft-tissue mass with eggshell calcification, not a systemic inflammatory syndrome with an elevated ESR.

educationalObjective: Polymyalgia rheumatica presents with proximal girdle pain and stiffness without weakness, elevated ESR/CRP, normal CK, and a rapid response to low-dose steroids in older women.

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 68-year-old woman with new shoulder and hip girdle stiffness has an ESR of 90 mm/h and a normal CK. She is started on low-dose prednisone and improves dramatically within days. Two weeks later she develops a new unilateral headache, pain in her jaw when chewing, and tenderness over her temple.
question: Which of the following best explains the relationship between her initial condition and this new complication?

options.text: Both conditions are caused by anti-Jo-1 antibodies
Her initial illness was actually dermatomyositis with an occult malignancy
She has developed Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
Polymyalgia rheumatica is associated with giant cell arteritis, which can cause blindness
She has IgG4-related disease with autoimmune aortitis

explanation_correct: Polymyalgia rheumatica is closely associated with giant cell (temporal) arteritis. Her new unilateral headache, jaw claudication, and temporal tenderness signal giant cell arteritis, which risks blindness from anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. Giant cell arteritis shows granulomatous inflammation of the temporal, vertebral, and ophthalmic arteries with markedly elevated ESR/CRP, and requires high-dose glucocorticoids before biopsy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Anti-Jo-1 is a histidyl-tRNA synthetase antibody associated with polymyositis, not polymyalgia rheumatica or giant cell arteritis.
explanation_incorrect.B: Dermatomyositis features proximal weakness, CK elevation, and characteristic rashes; it does not explain temporal headache and jaw claudication.
explanation_incorrect.C: Lambert-Eaton is a neuromuscular junction disorder with proximal weakness and autonomic symptoms, unrelated to an elevated ESR or temporal arteritis.
explanation_incorrect.E: IgG4-related aortitis can affect the aorta but does not produce the classic temporal arteritis picture of jaw claudication and temporal tenderness linked to polymyalgia rheumatica.

educationalObjective: Recognize the polymyalgia rheumatica–giant cell arteritis association and the warning signs of giant cell arteritis (headache, jaw claudication, blindness risk).

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 34-year-old woman has had 8 months of widespread musculoskeletal pain involving both sides of her body, along with fatigue, nonrestorative sleep, and difficulty concentrating described as 'fibro fog.' Examination shows multiple tender points on palpation but no joint swelling, weakness, or neurologic deficits. ESR and CK are normal.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Fibromyalgia is most common in females 20–50 years old and causes chronic widespread pain with tender points, stiffness, paresthesias, poor sleep, fatigue, and cognitive disturbance ('fibro fog'). Inflammatory markers such as ESR are normal, which distinguishes it from polymyalgia rheumatica and the myositides.

explanation_incorrect.B: Polymyalgia rheumatica occurs in patients older than 50 with proximal girdle pain, fever and weight loss, and an elevated ESR/CRP.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polymyositis causes true proximal weakness, an elevated CK, and endomysial inflammation rather than tender points with normal CK.
explanation_incorrect.D: Systemic lupus erythematosus can cause arthralgias and fatigue but usually has serologies such as ANA and anti-dsDNA plus other organ involvement, not tender points with normal inflammatory markers.
explanation_incorrect.E: Myositis ossificans follows blunt trauma with a painful mass and eggshell calcification, not chronic widespread pain.

educationalObjective: Fibromyalgia is chronic widespread pain with tender points and normal inflammatory markers in young-to-middle-aged women.

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 41-year-old woman has widespread pain, tender points, fatigue, and poor sleep. ESR, CK, and ANA are all normal. She asks about treatment options for her condition.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this patient?

options.text: Regular aerobic exercise, SNRIs or TCAs, and gabapentinoids

explanation_correct: Fibromyalgia is managed with regular exercise plus neuromodulatory analgesics such as tricyclic antidepressants, SNRIs, and gabapentinoids. Because there is no systemic inflammation, immunosuppressive therapy is not indicated.

explanation_incorrect.A: High-dose glucocorticoids are used for giant cell arteritis and other vasculitides, not for fibromyalgia, which has normal inflammatory markers.
explanation_incorrect.B: Cyclophosphamide is reserved for severe vasculitis such as granulomatosis with polyangiitis or polyarteritis nodosa, not a noninflammatory pain syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.D: Pyridostigmine is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used to treat myasthenia gravis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Smoking cessation is the definitive treatment for Buerger disease, not fibromyalgia.

educationalObjective: Fibromyalgia is treated with exercise and neuromodulatory analgesics, not immunosuppression.

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 55-year-old woman develops progressive symmetric weakness of the shoulder girdle over 3 months. She has difficulty lifting her arms and rising from a chair. There are no skin rashes. CK is markedly elevated, ANA is positive, and anti-Jo-1 antibodies are detected. Muscle biopsy shows endomysial inflammation with CD8+ T cells.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Polymyositis causes progressive symmetric proximal muscle weakness, most often involving the shoulders, with an elevated CK, positive ANA, and myositis-specific antibodies such as anti-Jo-1 (histidyl-tRNA synthetase). Biopsy shows endomysial inflammation with CD8+ T cells, and there are no cutaneous findings.

explanation_incorrect.A: Polymyalgia rheumatica causes pain and stiffness without weakness and has a normal CK.
explanation_incorrect.B: Fibromyalgia has widespread pain and tender points with a normal CK and no true weakness.
explanation_incorrect.C: Myositis ossificans is a post-traumatic painful mass with metaplastic bone formation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Lambert-Eaton is a neuromuscular junction disorder with presynaptic calcium channel antibodies, autonomic symptoms, and improvement with use, not an elevated CK or endomysial inflammation.

educationalObjective: Polymyositis presents with proximal weakness, elevated CK, anti-Jo-1, and endomysial CD8+ inflammation without a rash.

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 60-year-old man has 2 months of progressive proximal weakness and a violet-blue swelling of the eyelids. Examination shows flat-topped papules over the metacarpophalangeal joints, a photodistributed rash over the face and shoulders, and thickened, cracked skin on the fingertips described as 'mechanic's hands.' CK is elevated.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Dermatomyositis presents with proximal weakness plus characteristic skin findings: Gottron papules, heliotrope (violaceous) edema of the eyelids, a 'shawl and face' photodistributed rash, and mechanic's hands. It features perimysial inflammation with CD4+ T cells and an increased risk of occult malignancy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Polymyositis has similar proximal weakness but lacks the pathognomonic rash and has endomysial CD8+ inflammation rather than perimysial CD4+ inflammation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Systemic lupus erythematosus can cause a malar rash and serositis but not Gottron papules and heliotrope eyelid edema with this pattern.
explanation_incorrect.D: Polymyalgia rheumatica has no weakness, rash, or CK elevation.
explanation_incorrect.E: Fibromyalgia has no weakness, rash, or elevated CK.

educationalObjective: Dermatomyositis is distinguished from polymyositis by its characteristic rashes and increased risk of occult malignancy.

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 48-year-old woman with proximal muscle weakness, an elevated CK, and interstitial lung disease undergoes testing for myositis-specific autoantibodies.
question: Which of the following autoantibodies is directed against histidyl-tRNA synthetase and is associated with polymyositis?
explanation_correct: Anti-Jo-1 is directed against histidyl-tRNA synthetase and is the classic myositis-specific antibody associated with polymyositis, often with interstitial lung disease. Anti-SRP targets the signal recognition particle and anti-Mi-2 targets a helicase; ANA is a nonspecific finding.

explanation_incorrect.A: Anti-SRP is directed against the signal recognition particle, not histidyl-tRNA synthetase.
explanation_incorrect.B: Anti-Mi-2 targets a helicase and is more strongly associated with dermatomyositis.
explanation_incorrect.C: ANA is a nonspecific screening antibody and is not directed against histidyl-tRNA synthetase.
explanation_incorrect.E: Anti-C1q is associated with hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis, not polymyositis.

educationalObjective: Anti-Jo-1 is the histidyl-tRNA synthetase autoantibody associated with polymyositis.

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 19-year-old football player sustains blunt trauma to his thigh. Over the next several weeks a painful soft-tissue mass develops in the quadriceps. Radiographs show a peripheral 'eggshell' calcification, and biopsy reveals metaplastic bone surrounding an area of fibroblastic proliferation.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: Myositis ossificans is heterotopic ossification involving skeletal muscle, often the quadriceps, after blunt muscle trauma. It presents as a painful soft-tissue mass with eggshell calcification on imaging and metaplastic bone around fibroblastic proliferation on histology. It is benign but may be mistaken for sarcoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: Rhabdomyosarcoma is a malignant tumor without the post-traumatic eggshell calcification or benign metaplastic bone formation.
explanation_incorrect.B: Polymyositis is an inflammatory cause of proximal weakness with an elevated CK, not a trauma-associated mass.
explanation_incorrect.D: Dermatomyositis includes proximal weakness and characteristic rashes rather than a localized post-traumatic mass.
explanation_incorrect.E: Fibromyalgia is widespread pain with tender points and no calcification or mass.

educationalObjective: Myositis ossificans is benign post-traumatic heterotopic bone formation in muscle that can mimic sarcoma.

subject: Musculoskeletal
subtopic: Polymyalgia rheumatica, fibromyalgia, myositis, IgG4-related disease
vignette: A 57-year-old man has painless enlargement of his salivary and lacrimal glands, a diffusely enlarged thyroid, and imaging showing a sausage-shaped pancreas. Serum IgG4 is markedly elevated. He also has hydronephrosis due to retroperitoneal fibrosis.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this patient's underlying disease process?

options.text: IgG4-related disease with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration
Giant cell arteritis with granulomatous inflammation

explanation_correct: IgG4-related disease is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition characterized by fibrosis and a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with elevated serum IgG4. It causes sialadenitis and dacryoadenitis, Riedel thyroiditis, autoimmune pancreatitis, autoimmune aortitis, and retroperitoneal fibrosis that can obstruct the ureters and cause hydronephrosis or acute kidney injury.

explanation_incorrect.B: Giant cell arteritis is a granulomatous large-vessel arteritis in older women with headache and jaw claudication, not multiorgan fibrosis with a high IgG4.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polymyalgia rheumatica is proximal girdle pain with an elevated ESR in older patients, not glandular enlargement or pancreatic and retroperitoneal fibrosis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Dermatomyositis has proximal weakness and rashes with a malignancy risk, not elevated IgG4 or fibrosis.
explanation_incorrect.E: IgA vasculitis is a childhood post-URI purpuric rash with arthralgias and abdominal pain.

educationalObjective: IgG4-related disease causes multiorgan fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates with elevated serum IgG4.
